source.title: Network size and weights size for memorization with two-layers neural networks
source.authors: Sébastien Bubeck; Ronen Eldan; Yin Lee; Dan Mikulincer

page_placements.theme: Constructive arbitrary-label capacity has explicit constraints

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; some equations contain formatting or OCR artifacts, but the relevant statements are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves memorization results for two-layer ReLU networks using explicit constructions and an NTK construction. These bear on fitting arbitrary labels, but do not reproduce training standard deep networks with stochastic gradient methods.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical existence and construction results, not experimental training runs. Its cited account of SGD memorization from Zhang et al. is prior work and is not recorded as a result here.
record.test_reason: The paper proves representational capacity and guarantees for purpose-built memorization constructions. It does not establish random-label fitting by standard networks trained with stochastic gradient methods, or test any other listed version. Its discussion of SGD memorization cites prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors establish compact two-layer ReLU memorization constructions and a harmonic construction with nearly optimal total weight under stated assumptions. The harmonic guarantee permits excluding some data points and gives approximate fitting.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes explicit two-layer ReLU memorization constructions, including an NTK-regime construction; it does not reproduce the cited deep-network SGD experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The guarantees depend on data assumptions: general position for Proposition 4, genericity for the NTK result, and bounded pairwise inner products and label conditions for the harmonic result.

fits_no_version.finding: Two-layer ReLU networks admit exact arbitrary-label interpolation in general position, approximate NTK memorization under genericity assumptions, and a harmonic construction combining compact size with nearly optimal total weight.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Two-layer networks have sufficient representational capacity for arbitrary-label memorization under stated data assumptions, with construction-dependent width and weight guarantees.

record.problems: The claim-relevant results are theoretical construction guarantees rather than empirical training results. The tested networks are two-layer, and the data assumptions and guarantees differ across results; the paper does not report the claim’s test-error or true-label generalization comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version results were reported. Cited results about SGD memorization, including Zhang et al. (2017), are prior work and were excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting by standard deep networks using stochastic gradient methods, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and chance test performance.
Training-time comparison between true and random labels, including dependence on corruption fraction.
Training the same networks to zero error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily degrading test performance across label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy labels during training.

record.verdict_notes: The absence of SGD experiments does not challenge V1 or limit its scope; these constructions answer a different question. Likewise, total-weight bounds alone do not test the explicit regularizers named in V5.

versions.untested_parts: The paper establishes fitting arbitrary labels under stated data assumptions, but does not test completely random image labels, test error at chance, SGD training, unchanged training hyperparameters, or generalization on true labels.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network (Proposition 4)
rows.operation_detail: Proves existence of a network that exactly memorizes arbitrary real labels for data in general position.

conditions.value: in general position in R^d; any hyperplane contains at most d points

rows.note: An existence result for a two-layer ReLU network; no training procedure or test-set result is reported.
rows.check: Proposition 4 correctly guarantees exact interpolation with 4⌈n/d⌉ ReLU neurons in general position. Existence of specially constructed weights does not measure the SGD-trained behavior named in V1.

rows.subject: NTK network (Theorems 2–3)
rows.operation_detail: Gives an NTK-regime construction with expected relative training error at most ε.

conditions.value: over random initialization of the main weights

rows.measure: Expected squared training error relative to squared label norm.
rows.note: The theorem states an approximate memorization guarantee; it does not report SGD training time or test error.
rows.check: Theorem 2 guarantees expected relative squared fitting error for an iterative NTK construction that adds neurons. Theorem 3 supplies its building block. Neither establishes V1's standard SGD training behavior.

rows.subject: harmonic network (Theorem 5)
rows.operation_detail: Constructs a ReLU network with approximate fit on a subset of the labeled data.

conditions.value: unit vectors with |xi·xj| ≤ γ for i ≠ j

rows.measure: Expected squared error on A and number of fitted indices.
rows.note: The guarantee is approximate and applies to a subset A; the theorem does not guarantee fitting every point.
rows.check: The construction does not measure V1. The extracted formulas are also wrong: Theorem 5 gives |A| ≥ n − 1/γ²; the expression involving log(1/ε)√(nγ²d)/ε bounds total weight, not excluded indices. Its proof gives width proportional to nγ²[log(n)]^(m²+m)log(1/ε)/ε, rather than the recorded inverse-power expression. Include the assumption nγ^(m−2) ≤ 1/2.

source_check.correct: E[‖f_A − y_A‖²] ≤ ε‖y‖²; |A| ≥ n − 1/γ². Width k = ⌈C_m γ² n log(n)^(m²+m) log(1/ε)/ε⌉. Total weight W(f) = Õ((log(1/ε)/ε)√(nγ²d)). Theorem 5 additionally requires nγ^(m−2) ≤ 1/2.
source_check.locator_found: Section 5, Theorem 5, equations (15)–(16), p. 12; proof, p. 13.
source_check.problem: The excluded-index formula incorrectly uses the total-weight bound; the attached width formula is also incorrect.

relation.reason: Section 2 discusses prior observations of SGD memorization and their generalization implications; its own results concern different memorization constructions.

tranche.reason: The study establishes capacity and purpose-built memorization constructions, without testing any version's specified behavior under standard stochastic-gradient training.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased. The harmonic guarantee permits excluding points and provides approximate fitting; it does not establish V1.
